messages:
maria: heads-up — while onboarding hf/emoji-spm-1 i hit a nasty SPM->BPE conversion edge. some emoji zwj sequences and nonbreaking-space variants end up remapped to existing token ids after our merge rewrite. outputs look fine on tokenized level but decoded text is garbled and eval BLEU/ROUGE drop is consistent across runs.

jon: can you paste the conversion command and a minimal repro?

maria: sure. here's the convert command we run in the harness:

```bash
python tools/convert_spm_to_bpe.py 
  --hf-repo hf/emoji-spm-1 
  --out-dir /tmp/converted 
  --preserve-special-tokens true 
  --merge-strategy canonicalize
```

example tokenization mismatch: input = hi<ZWJ>👩‍🚀 (zwj between hi and emoji)
spm tokenize => [345, 12, 981]
our converted bpe => [345, 12, 345]  # id 345 reused, collision

also noticed config.json reports vocab_size 50257 but converted vocab ends up 50256 after a merge collapse, so offsets shift for reserved tokens.

leo: ugh, that's the NBSP / ZWJ normalization gotcha. hf model used NFKC normalization in the SPM training, but our conversion pipeline canonicalizes differently (NFC). that changes piece boundaries for ligatures and zwj sequences. plus some emoji sequences include invisible joiners which SPM kept as separate pieces. when the merge pass dedups merges it ends up remapping indices.

tara: this would explain tied regressions after quantization too — if token ids change, the embedding table alignment is off and quantized weights point at wrong tokens. did you try a non-quantized float run to confirm?

maria: yes. float32 generation with converted vocab already shows word-level corruption. 4-bit per-channel q8_0 makes it several tokens worse. benchmark summary (toy):

- baseline hf model (native spm): ppl 12.3, exact-match 0.74
- converted float: ppl 13.0, exact-match 0.69
- converted q4_0: ppl 15.5, exact-match 0.61

jon: can you dump the special_tokens_map and the first 64 vocab entries pre/post conversion? we should check if reserved tokens like  and pad shifted. also add a small unit test that tokenizes these canonical zwj/emoji strings and asserts id equality.

maria: pasted snippets in Gist: link here -> https://gist.example/emoji-spm-diffs (includes before/after lists and minimal script)

leo: two concrete fixes to try: 1) run the spm tokenizer with the same unicode normalization as the model's original training (NFKC) before conversion; 2) when collapsing merges, keep placeholders for reserved tokens and reassign any removed indices to end of vocab to preserve offsets. both are non-trivial but doable.

tara: also watch chat templates — some of our templates rely on a placeholder token sequence like  that gets tokenized differently if normalization changes. that made a canary chat test fail fast in my last rollout. add a chat-template tokenization check to the onboarding eval.

jon: +1 on tests. i'll add a conversion check that runs: tokenization id parity, decode parity for short strings, and a fallback that rebuilds merges using the huggingface tokenizer to preserve exact piece ordering.

maria: quick workaround for the immediate customer demo: pinned the converted vocab and forced mapping of special tokens back to original indices in the model config. it's hacky but restored demo quality. still need a proper fix for the pipeline.

deploy-bot: reminder — please open an eng-infra ticket if you need infra for large regen runs.

jon: i'll own creating the ticket and push a branch with unit tests + fix proposals. tagging @tara and @leo for review.

maria: thanks. adding repro artifacts to the onboarding folder and a short note on the conversion README about zwj/nbsp pitfalls. :eyes:
